newsitem.title: USA: Rock-Tenn, Sonoco to merge divisions.
newsitem.headline: Rock-Tenn, Sonoco to merge divisions.

text.p: Rock-Tenn Co and Sonoco Products Co said on Wednesday that the companies agreed to merge their fiber partition businesses into a new joint venture company with about $150 million in combined annual sales.
Solid fiber partitions are used to separate and protect products during shipping, the companies said in a joint statement.
Both companies cited the consolidating glass industry and overcapacity in the market as reasons for the venture.

Rock-Tenn and Sonoco said Rock-Tenn is contributing its eight fiber partition plants and machine engineering facility to the venture. These facilities generated about $100 million in sales for the year ended September 30, 1996, the companies said.
Sonoco is contributing its six fiber partition plants in the United States and its fiber partition plant in Mexico to the joint venture, generating $50 million in sales for 1996.
Under the terms of the agreement, Rock-Tenn will own 65 percent of the joint venture and Sonoco will own 35 percent, the companies said.
Management of the venture will be under the direction of a five-member managing board with three Rock-Tenn representatives and two from Sonoco, the companies said.

Consummation of the joint venture is subject to satisfaction of a number of conditions including negotiation and execution of a definitive joint venture agreement, obtaining certain regulatory approvals and the satisfactory completion of due diligence, the companies said.
Closing of the deal is expected in the first quarter of 1997, the companies said.
